description: Build the UI layer (HomePage, LandedPage, ContactUsPage, PrimaryNavigationComponent) and the UI test suite: homepage title, primary navigation visible, navigation reaching the About Us page, and the enquiry form's mandatory-field contract plus value retention - with NO submit method anywhere, because the target is a production site. Also wires the per-scenario WebDriver lifecycle hooks and failure-artefact capture into the UI suite. Depends on FEAT-001 for ElementWaits, ScenarioDriver, WebDriverFactory and FailureArtefacts. Independent of FEAT-002.
steps: Open EVERY page object and component with the same documented-exception header comment: this is a third-party WordPress site with no data-testid attributes and we cannot add any, so locators are the most stable selectors actually available; this is a deliberate documented exception to ui-automation-selenium.md section 1; on KEYinfinity data-testid becomes the primary strategy again; and any XPath must carry its own inline justification. Methods are SYNCHRONOUS with no *Async suffix because Selenium's C# API is synchronous, locators are private static readonly By fields built from named consts, an IWebElement is never cached in a field, nothing asserts, and IWebDriver plus ElementWaits arrive by constructor injection.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\src\QAAutomation.UI\Components\PrimaryNavigationComponent.cs with private static readonly By HeaderNavigation = By.CssSelector("nav.site-header__navigation"). Expose IsVisible() and FollowLink(string linkText). Both resolve the navigation through ElementWaits.WaitUntilFirstVisible, then FollowLink scopes FindElements(By.CssSelector("a")) to that element and uses a foreach comparing trimmed link text, clicking the first match that is Displayed and throwing NoSuchElementException with a plain-English message naming the link if none matched. Add a comment explaining there are TWO site-header__navigation elements in the DOM, a desktop copy and a mobile copy, only one of which is displayed at 1920x1080, so a bare FindElement could resolve a hidden link and throw ElementNotInteractableException.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\src\QAAutomation.UI\Pages\HomePage.cs with Open() navigating to SiteOptions.BaseUrl and waiting for the navigation to be visible, ReadTitle(), a Navigation property exposing the component, and FollowNavigationLinkTo(string linkText) returning a LandedPage. Add a comment stating the homepage hero carousel and the animated statistic counters are deliberately never exposed by this page object, and that there are four <h1> elements on the page - one per carousel slide - so no heading assertion is offered.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\src\QAAutomation.UI\Pages\LandedPage.cs - a deliberately thin page object for wherever the navigation took us, exposing ReadTitle() and ReadCurrentUrl(). It keeps the journey readable without demanding a page object per marketing page; say so in a comment.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\src\QAAutomation.UI\Pages\ContactUsPage.cs with Open() navigating to SiteOptions.BaseUrl + SiteOptions.ContactPagePath. Hold a private static readonly array of field-name-to-By pairs built from named consts for all eight fields - input_2_5 First Name, input_2_19 Surname, input_2_6 Postcode, input_2_7 Email address, input_2_8 Telephone, input_2_4 Company Name, input_2_9 Mobile, input_2_10 Your Enquiry - with a comment explaining Gravity Forms renders deterministic input_<formId>_<fieldId> ids and that form 2 is the enquiry form. Expose IsFieldMandatory(string fieldName) which resolves the field through ElementWaits and reads its aria-required attribute, TypeInto(string fieldName, string value) and ReadValueOf(string fieldName). Resolve a field name to its locator with an explicit foreach and throw a plain-English exception naming the unknown field.

Give ContactUsPage a prominent multi-line header comment, above the locator block, stating: this is a PRODUCTION website and this page object is READ-ONLY; a successful form submit creates a real sales enquiry for Landmark Systems; the live form carries the HTML novalidate attribute so there is NO client-side validation to assert and the only validation is server-side behind an AJAX POST; and therefore this class deliberately has NO submit method and none may be added, so that nobody can 'finish' the scenario later.
Create d:\git\QAAutomation\src\QAAutomation.UI\UiRegistration.cs with AddPageObjects(IServiceCollection) registering PrimaryNavigationComponent, HomePage, LandedPage and ContactUsPage as scoped.

Create the test project wiring at d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.UI: reqnroll.json with { "language": { "feature": "en-GB" } }; AssemblyInfo.cs with [assembly: Parallelizable(ParallelScope.Fixtures)] and [assembly: LevelOfParallelism(2)] - one browser per worker, two workers, per the brief; SiteNavigationContext.cs (PageTitle, LandedUrl, NavigationVisible) and EnquiryFormContext.cs (FieldIsMandatory, ValueHeldByField); and UiScenarioDependencies.cs with a static [ScenarioDependencies] factory calling TestConfigurationLoader.Load(), AddTestConfiguration, AddBrowserSupport, AddPageObjects and registering both contexts scoped. Register NO API client - suite separation is structural.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.UI\WebDriverHooks.cs as a [Binding] class with ScenarioDriver, FailureArtefacts and ScenarioContext injected through the constructor. [BeforeScenario(Order = 10)] calls ScenarioDriver.Start(). [AfterScenario(Order = 100)] captures artefacts inside a try when ScenarioContext.TestError is not null, and calls ScenarioDriver.Quit() in the finally, so a capture failure can never leak a chromedriver or browser process. No assertions in hooks, no early return before the quit, and never log a cookie, token or unmasked PII in hook diagnostics.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.UI\Features\Homepage.feature with feature-level tags @ui @regression @marketing and a comment stating the rotating hero carousel and the animated statistic counters are deliberately never asserted on, and that the page has four <h1> elements for the same reason. Scenarios: (@smoke) 'The home page identifies the product in its page title' - Given the visitor opens the Landmark home page / Then the browser page title is the expected home page title. 'The home page shows the primary navigation' - Given the visitor opens the Landmark home page / Then the primary navigation is visible.

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.UI\Features\PrimaryNavigation.feature with feature-level tags @ui @regression @marketing and one scenario, 'The About Us navigation link opens the About Us page': Given the visitor opens the Landmark home page / When the visitor follows the "About Us" link in the primary navigation / Then the browser page title mentions "About Us".

Create d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.UI\Features\EnquiryForm.feature with feature-level tags @ui @regression @marketing, opening with the same read-only warning as the page object in Gherkin comments: production site, a successful submit creates a real sales enquiry, the form carries novalidate so there is no client-side validation to assert, ContactUsPage deliberately has no submit method, and this scenario therefore proves the same mandatory-field rule without a write. Then a Scenario Outline 'The enquiry form declares which of its fields are mandatory' - Given the visitor opens the Landmark contact page / Then the "<fieldName>" field is mandatory: <mandatory> - with 'Examples: mandatory and optional fields (equivalence partitions)' and exactly four rows: First Name true, Email address true, Company Name false, Your Enquiry false. Then a scenario 'The enquiry form holds the details the visitor types without submitting them': Given the visitor opens the Landmark contact page / When the visitor types "Automated test enquiry - please ignore" into the "Your Enquiry" field / Then the "Your Enquiry" field holds "Automated test enquiry - please ignore".

Create Steps\HomepageSteps.cs, Steps\PrimaryNavigationSteps.cs and Steps\EnquiryFormSteps.cs as plain void bindings - Selenium is synchronous, so there is nothing to await and no Task.Run. Constructor injection only, one or two page-object calls then an assertion, and no assertion inside any Given. Read the expected home page title from SiteOptions.HomePageTitle rather than a literal in the step. In the navigation step call ElementWaits.WaitUntilTitleContains before reading the title so the assertion is not racing the page load. No By locators, CSS, XPath, FindElement, IWebDriver or WebDriverWait may appear in any step file.
acceptance_criteria: dotnet build d:\git\QAAutomation\QAAutomation.sln reports 0 Warning(s) and 0 Error(s).
dotnet test d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.UI passes all 8 scenarios headless with 0 failed and 0 skipped.
After the UI run, Get-Process chromedriver -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue returns nothing, proving teardown quit every driver.

Forcing one UI assertion to fail produces d:\git\QAAutomation\test-results\<suite>\<scenario>-<timestamp>\ containing screenshot.png, page-source.html, console.log and location.txt; restoring the assertion returns the suite to green.
ContactUsPage contains no submit method, no Click on a submit control and no form POST, and both the page object and the feature file carry the explicit read-only comment.
No step definition file contains a By locator, CSS selector, XPath, FindElement, IWebDriver, WebDriverWait, Thread.Sleep or LINQ.
verification: Get-Process chromedriver -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue - must return nothing after the run

Temporarily break one expected title, run dotnet test d:\git\QAAutomation\tests\QAAutomation.Tests.UI, confirm the four artefact files exist under d:\git\QAAutomation\test-results, then restore the title and re-run green
findings:
SURPRISE 1 - THE BIGGEST ONE. THE CONTACT FORM FIELDS ARE NOT 'DISPLAYED' ON THE PLAIN /contact-us/ ADDRESS, AND FEAT-004 MUST KNOW THIS IF IT EVER TOUCHES THAT PAGE. The site wraps the form in <div class="form-container aos-init" data-aos="fade-up">. AOS (animate-on-scroll) holds a data-aos element at opacity 0 until it scrolls into view, at which point it adds the aos-animate class. Selenium's displayedness check treats a zero-opacity element as NOT displayed, so ElementWaits.WaitUntilVisible(By.Id("input_2_5")) times out after the full 20 seconds even though every input_2_* id is present in the page source. First run: 5 of 8 scenarios failed exactly this way, all five from EnquiryForm.feature, all with 'Timed out after 20 seconds' thrown from ElementWaits.WaitUntilVisible via ContactUsPage.Open(). FIX: ContactUsPage.Open() navigates to Site:BaseUrl + Site:ContactPagePath + the const FormSectionAnchor = "#form" - the page's own anchor, the same target its 'COMPLETE FORM' button links to. The browser lands on the form section during load, AOS reveals it, and the wait returns immediately. Verified: 5/5 enquiry-form cases pass. The reasoning is written out in full in a long comment on Open() because the failure mode is genuinely baffling otherwise.

SURPRISE 2 - A 10-SECOND NEWSLETTER MODAL THAT COVERS THE WHOLE VIEWPORT. The theme's main.min.js contains subscribeModal() with DELAY_MS = 10000: ten seconds after load it adds is-visible to <div class="modal-overlay" id="subscribe-modal">, whose CSS is position:fixed; inset:0; z-index:10000; background:rgba(255,255,255,.5). It is suppressed only by a localStorage key (landmark_subscribe_modal_closed_at) for one hour, and every scenario gets a fresh browser, so IT WILL ALWAYS APPEAR about ten seconds in. Consequences, which FEAT-004 inherits: (a) ANY CLICK on the contact page later than ~10s after load will be refused with ElementClickInterceptedException; (b) reading an attribute and SendKeys/Clear keep working while it is up, which is why the read-only enquiry scenarios are unaffected; (c) this is the second reason Open() uses the #form anchor rather than clicking 'COMPLETE FORM' - no click means no race against that timer; (d) if an E2E scenario ever needs a click on a slow-loading page, close the modal through .modal-content--close-button first and then ElementWaits.WaitUntilGone on .modal-overlay (the overlay goes to visibility:hidden, so WaitUntilGone works on it), but do NOT wait for the modal unconditionally - on a fast page it is not up yet and the wait would burn 20 seconds. There is also a CookieYes banner bottom-left (.cky-consent-container) whose full-screen overlay ships as 'cky-overlay cky-hide', i.e. hidden, so it intercepts nothing and is deliberately left alone.

SURPRISE 3 - THE 'About Us' NAV CLICK AND THE HOME PAGE TITLE BOTH WORKED FIRST TIME. ElementWaits.WaitUntilFirstVisible on nav.site-header__navigation handled the duplicated desktop/mobile navigation exactly as FEAT-001 intended; no ElementNotInteractableException was ever seen. The configured Site:HomePageTitle matched the live DOM title exactly, so 'Should().Be(...)' is safe for the home page - only the LANDED page titles need 'Contain', because those are SEO titles.

SURPRISE 4 - dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~..." IS CASE-SENSITIVE AND MATCHES THE GENERATED CLASS NAME, NOT THE FILE NAME. Reqnroll names the generated fixture from the FEATURE TITLE, not the .feature file name. Homepage.feature has 'Feature: Home page', so the class is HomePageFeature and '--filter "FullyQualifiedName~Homepage"' matches NOTHING ('No test matches the given testcase filter'). Use HomePageFeature. Worth putting in the README's 'running a subset' section.

SELENIUM API NOTES. IWebElement.GetDomAttribute("aria-required") is used to read the mandatory declaration (the HTML attribute) and GetDomProperty("value") to read what was typed (the live DOM property, because the value ATTRIBUTE only ever shows the markup's starting value). Both are the modern Selenium 4 methods and neither produces an obsolescence warning on 4.50.0, so the build stays at 0 warnings. An optional field carries no aria-required attribute at all, so GetDomAttribute returns null and IsFieldMandatory treats null as false with a comment saying so.

THINGS FEAT-004 CAN REUSE OR MUST AVOID.
- WebDriverHooks.cs can be copied verbatim into Tests.E2E with the namespace changed and SuiteName changed to "e2e" - the plan already says to duplicate rather than share. Same for ContainerStartup.cs, though E2E has no Parallelizable attribute so the cold-start race is less likely; copy it anyway, it costs nothing.
- UiScenarioDependencies is the shape to follow: AddTestConfiguration, AddBrowserSupport, AddPageObjects, then the scoped contexts. E2E additionally needs AddApiClients(testConfiguration.Api) AND services.AddScoped<ScenarioCorrelation>() - except that AddBrowserSupport ALREADY registers ScenarioCorrelation, so E2E must not register it twice; calling AddBrowserSupport is enough to satisfy RequestContextHandler's dependency.
- STEP PHRASES ALREADY TAKEN BY THE UI ASSEMBLY (a different assembly from Tests.E2E, so E2E may safely reuse the wording, but it must define its own bindings): "the visitor opens the Landmark home page", "the browser page title is the expected home page title", "the primary navigation is visible", "the visitor follows the {string} link in the primary navigation", "the browser page title mentions {string}", "the visitor opens the Landmark contact page", the regex '^the ""(.*)"" field is mandatory: (true|false)$', "the visitor types {string} into the {string} field", "the {string} field holds {string}".
- Note that "the browser page title mentions {string}" is ALREADY USED by the UI suite. The E2E Then is 'the browser page title mentions the title the content API reported', which is different wording and will not clash even inside one assembly.
- LandedPage is the page object to reuse for 'open an arbitrary URL and read its title' - but it has no Open(string url) method, because nothing in the UI suite needed one. FEAT-004 will have to add one (and guard the URL with UrlHostChecker.HasSameHost before navigating, per the plan), or navigate in its own page object.
- A regex step binding works and converts "true"/"false" to a bool parameter with no custom transformation: [Then(@"^the ""(.*)"" field is mandatory: (true|false)$")] public void ...(string fieldName, bool expectedMandatory). Reqnroll treats an expression anchored with ^...$ as a regex rather than a cucumber expression. Useful if a {bool} placeholder is ever wanted; {bool} itself was not relied on.
- ElementWaits IS INJECTED INTO ONE STEP CLASS (PrimaryNavigationSteps) to call WaitUntilTitleContains before reading a title, exactly as FEAT-003 step 13 specifies. That keeps the wait in the one shared helper while leaving no By, driver, WebDriverWait, FindElement, Thread.Sleep or LINQ in any step file (verified by Select-String). FEAT-004's Then on the browser title should do the same so its assertion does not race the page load.
